question: Should OpenClaw core own durable signed publisher-follow state and its CLI lifecycle, or should publisher subscriptions remain an extension/ClawHub-owned capability until a generic core contract is approved?
rationale: This PR adds a persistent core data model, CLI surface, and trust boundary; correctness review cannot decide the long-term ownership and supported user contract without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Sponsor a core lifecycle
options.body: Approve core ownership and require the focused upgrade proof, public command/config docs, and current-head runtime evidence before merge.

options.title: Keep it extension-oriented
options.body: Pause this stacked core feature and define the minimum generic plugin or ClawHub seam required for publisher-follow behavior outside core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve core ownership and require the focused upgrade proof, public command/config docs, and current-head runtime evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only evidence-backed person connected to the full proposed publisher-feed stack; maintainer ownership history should be established before a final product decision.
